analysis.investment_thesis: INOX India is a genuine niche dominator in cryogenic equipment with powerful secular tailwinds — LNG infrastructure, green hydrogen, and India's space programme — but at 53x earnings with a PEG ratio north of 2.5x, the market has already priced in years of perfect execution. Great business, wrong price for a new position.
key_strengths: Niche moat in cryogenic machinery — high technical barriers, 56% gross margins, and ROCE of 38% signal real pricing power
Near-debt-free balance sheet (D/E: 0.10) with 5/5 years of positive OCF, giving optionality to fund expansion without dilution
Multi-decade tailwind convergence: LNG distribution, green hydrogen infra, and ISRO/private space cryogenic propulsion all in one product portfolio
key_risks: PEG ratio ~2.7x (P/E 53.5 ÷ ~20% earnings CAGR) — Lynch's ceiling is 1.0x, so the stock is priced for flawless execution with no margin of error
Free cash flow turned negative in FY25 (−₹3 Cr) as capex surged to ₹125 Cr — capital intensity is rising just as growth expectations are baked into valuation
Six-year net profit CAGR of only 2.7% reveals lumpy earnings history; if the hydrogen/LNG order cycle disappoints, multiple compression from 53x could be severe
red_flags: PEG ~2.7x is well above Lynch's hard limit of 1.5x — the growth story is real but fully priced
FCF went negative in FY25 despite ₹226 Cr net profit — a gap between accounting earnings and cash reality
Net profit CAGR (6Y) of just 2.7% vs. 12.3% revenue CAGR suggests historical margin/one-time income volatility that the current premium ignores
analysis.detailed_analysis:
INOX India is the kind of niche business I love to find — a 50-year-old company making highly specialised cryogenic tanks that nobody else in India does as well, serving a dozen end markets from beer kegs to rocket engines. The financials confirm the moat: 56% gross margins and 38% ROCE don't lie. Revenue has accelerated nicely from ₹966 Cr (FY23) to ₹1,306 Cr (FY25), a recent 3-year CAGR of ~16%, and earnings are running at ~20% over the same window. The balance sheet is clean, promoters own 75%, and every secular trend — LNG as a transition fuel, green hydrogen, India's space ambitions — puts INOX squarely in the flow.

The problem is a classic "good company, bad stock" situation at today's price. At 53x trailing earnings with ~15-20% growth, the PEG sits around 2.7x — more than double my comfort zone. I want to pay a dollar for a dollar of growth, not two and a half. Worse, free cash flow went slightly negative in FY25 as capex ramped to ₹125 Cr, meaning the company is now in an investment phase where earnings may not convert to cash for a year or two. If you already own it, hold — the business quality justifies patience. But chasing it at ₹1,492 means you're betting on multiple expansion or a jump to 25%+ growth, and I've learned that's not investing, that's hoping.
